subject: math

objective.text: Compare the length of two objects. Line up the endpoints so the comparison is fair.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Line up the endpoints
explanations.text: The endpoint is the very end of an object. To compare two objects, line up their endpoints. Start both objects at the same place. Then you can see which is longer.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (endpoints)

explanations.title: Hidden endpoints fool you
explanations.text: If you cannot see the endpoints, you cannot be sure. An object can look longer when it is held higher. Line up the endpoints first.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (marker and pencil, crayon and glue stick)

explanations.title: Say it with sentence frames
explanations.text: Use a sentence frame to tell what you see. The pencil is longer than the marker. The marker is shorter than the pencil.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (sentence frames)

explanations.title: Flipping does not change length
explanations.text: You can stand one object upside down. If the endpoints are still lined up, longer and shorter stay the same.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (flip an item upside down)

misconceptions.label: Higher top means longer
misconceptions.description: Child says the object whose top is higher is the longer one, even when the endpoints are hidden or not at the same place.
detection_signals: Says the marker is longer because its top is higher or taller, when the bottoms are not lined up.
Compares tops only and does not mention where the objects start.
misconceptions.response_text: Good looking! Let's check. Do both objects start at the same place? Line up the endpoints first. Then look again.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: The marker is longer because the top of it is taller)

assets_required.why_this_method: Two objects with exact relative lengths. The bottoms must line up exactly. Diffusion cannot keep lengths exact.
assets_required.description: A marker and a pencil. First they are held at different heights so the marker's top looks higher. Then both stand side by side on one floor line, and the pencil is clearly longer.
must_show_exactly: In the aligned state both bottoms touch the same floor line
In the aligned state the pencil's top is clearly higher than the marker's top
In the held state the marker is held higher so its top looks higher than the pencil's top
states_or_frames: State 1: held at different heights, marker top looks higher
State 2: both stand on the floor line, bottoms aligned, pencil longer
assets_required.interaction: Child can drag the marker down to the floor line. The bottoms then snap together. No typed input inside the widget.
assets_required.alt_text: A pencil and a marker standing side by side with their bottoms lined up.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat, simple pencil and marker standing side by side on a plain floor line, pencil taller, no text. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Two objects with exact relative lengths and a hide-and-reveal state. Anything exact and interactive is built by code.
assets_required.description: A crayon and a glue stick. First each is held in a fist so the endpoints are hidden. Then both stand side by side with bottoms aligned and the glue stick is clearly longer.
must_show_exactly: Exactly 2 objects: 1 crayon and 1 glue stick
Hidden state: each bottom endpoint is covered by a fist
Aligned state: both bottoms touch the same floor line
Aligned state: the glue stick's top is clearly higher than the crayon's top
states_or_frames: State 1: both in fists, endpoints hidden
State 2: both stand on the floor line, bottoms aligned, glue stick longer
assets_required.interaction: Child can open the fists. The objects then stand on the floor line. No typed input inside the widget.
assets_required.alt_text: A crayon and a glue stick, first hidden in two fists and then standing side by side.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
